newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentines believe Cavallo's charges - poll.
newsitem.headline: Argentines believe Cavallo's charges - poll.

text.p: Eighty-one percent of Argentines in the city of Buenos Aires believe former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo's accusations that two cabinet ministers covered up corruption and manipulated judges, according to a poll published Thursday.
The survey by pollster Ricardo Rouvier published in the daily El Cronista said that only five percent of respondents said Cavallo's charges were false, while 14 percent said they did not know.

The survey, based on 600 respondents in Buenos Aires, a traditionally opposed to the governing Peronist Party, also revealed an improvement in the image of the once "superminister" of Economy. Twenty-nine percent of respondents said they had a good or very good image of Cavallo.
Before being fired by President Carlos Menem almost three months ago, Cavallo's positive image had dropped below 20 percent, according to various surveys.
The new poll said that 32 percent feel his image is poor while 33 percent feel neither positive nor negative.
